title: European and Chinese exports kept growing despite the 2025 Trump trade shock
summary_en: Did the 2025 Trump tariff package disrupt global trade? Darvas and Lappe show that, despite an average US tariff hike to 16.8%, both EU and Chinese exports kept growing year-on-year — by redirecting away from the US toward ASEAN, the EU and other markets. China's exports to the US fell 45% but total Chinese exports still grew 6.6%; the EU showed similar resilience. The paper argues global trade is fragmenting (less US-centric) but not deglobalising.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for Hungarian export-led growth strategy (HIPA, KKM, NGM): the Hungarian export base — heavily integrated into EU automotive and electronics value chains — has limited direct US exposure but indirect exposure through EU-supply-chain partners. The paper supports keeping Hungarian export-promotion focus on intra-EU and ASEAN diversification rather than chasing US market share, and is useful input for the Hungarian export-strategy refresh under way at HIPA.
